hook: Falls now hurt India more than *road crashes*
hook_b: Falls now hurt India more than *road crashes*
tldr: A Lancet Regional Health–Southeast Asia study of GBD 2023 data ranks falls as India's top injury burden.

beats.what: Falls scored 958.7 DALYs per 1 lakh people in 2023, ahead of road injuries at 831.1 and self-harm at 671.9.
beats.why: India's ageing population is pushing up the total, even as rates adjusted for age have fallen.
beats.care: Older relatives at home face the biggest fall risk; roads remain the second biggest injury burden.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Road injury rates fell just 0.26% a year since 1990, the slowest among injury types studied.

cards.q: Which feels like the bigger risk in your family?

qs: What do Hyderabad homes and hospitals do to prevent falls among the elderly?

facts.t: Road injury deaths reached *1,68,000* in 2022, up *9.4%* from the year before.
The age-standardised fall rate is projected to drop *30.6%* by 2047, yet stay India's top injury burden.

viz.verdict: Falls have overtaken road crashes as the biggest injury burden.

learn.t: DALY = years of healthy life lost to early death or disability

watch: Whether road injury rates fall faster as vehicle ownership keeps rising.
